candidates.name: easy-host-cli-command-contract
candidates.description: Adds or changes easy-host commands while preserving the ten-command surface, stable exit codes, flag parity, JSON schemaVersion 1, TTY and NO_COLOR behavior, and secret-safe output.
candidates.reason: Ten commands and five read-only JSON payloads repeat the same fragile contract, and lifecycle handlers plus docs drift tests must consume it; no existing project package defines the exit-code, flag-parity, or output rules.

candidates.name: easy-host-registry-config
candidates.description: Creates or changes AppSpec TOML schema, defaults, name derivation, atomic registry writes, rebuildable state cache, env and secret merging, and key-named validation errors.
candidates.reason: Config and registry behavior repeats across add, update, status, and documentation, and mistakes risk data loss, secret leakage, or path traversal; no existing package covers this schema.

candidates.name: easy-host-prerequisite-doctor
candidates.description: Adds or changes doctor checks for Podman version and rootless mode, lingering, git, Node, disk, Railpack, and BuildKit with ordered pass, warn, fail, and remediation output under a no-network time budget.
candidates.reason: Doctor is composed by three features and two agents, and its version-window parsing, check ordering, JSON shape, and remediation lines are easy to drift; no existing package defines these invariants.

candidates.name: easy-host-container-runtime-contract
candidates.description: Wraps Podman and git calls with argument arrays, finite timeouts, labels, named volumes, restart policy, port publication, and redaction of secrets and URL credentials.
candidates.reason: Every runtime call shares security and safety rules repeated across app containers, buildkitd, and read commands; one package is needed to prevent shell interpolation, missing timeouts, or leaked environment values.

candidates.name: easy-host-health-gated-swap
candidates.description: Implements the stop, start, probe, keep or revert sequence shared by update and rollback, including phase reporting, bounded probes, previous-image restart, and state recording only after health.
candidates.reason: The swap is the highest-risk state transition and is reused by update and rollback; its revert and no-zero-container rules are fragile and currently spread across two feature documents.

candidates.name: easy-host-destructive-operation-safety
candidates.description: Guards remove and rollback with confirmation, per-app locks, label-scoped deletion, default volume retention, foreign-resource refusal, and two-image retention.
candidates.reason: Accidental data loss is the product's strongest prohibition and the rules repeat across remove, retention, volume deletion, and lock contention; no existing package encodes the confirmation and label-scoped deletion gates.

candidates.name: easy-host-build-layer
candidates.description: Pins and verifies Railpack, manages the rootless buildkitd lifecycle, builds a workspace into a timestamped image, streams output, and classifies unsupported-source, build, and infrastructure failures.
candidates.reason: The build layer is pre-1.0, digest-pinned, rootless-sensitive, and the top technical risk; its acquisition, daemon, streaming, and failure-classification rules repeat and are easy to regress.

candidates.name: easy-host-integration-gate
candidates.description: Adds gated Podman integration or release evidence with EASY_HOST_INTEGRATION enforcement, unique resources, local git fixtures, bounded waits, guaranteed cleanup, and non-vacuous assertions.
candidates.reason: Five integration suites and two human-review gates repeat the same gating, cleanup, and evidence discipline, and a silent skip would falsely certify the release.

candidates.name: easy-host-packaging-docs-sync
candidates.description: Keeps global install, packed tarball contents, generated shell completions, README, operations guides, and CLI and config references synchronized with the executable definitions.
candidates.reason: Packaging, completion generation, and reference documentation all drift from the same commander and zod sources; no existing package enforces the generated-from-source rule.

candidates.name: generic-typescript-cli-scaffold
candidates.description: Generic ESM TypeScript package, Biome, and Vitest scaffold conventions.
candidates.reason: Standard tooling conventions are already covered by the pinned stack and repository configuration; a project skill would duplicate framework guidance without protecting a product-specific invariant.

candidates.name: human-release-gate-automation
candidates.description: Automates the v0.1.0 success scenarios, including the real host reboot and manual LAN reachability check.
candidates.reason: The release gate is explicitly a human-review task that cannot be satisfied by automation; evidence collection belongs to easy-host-integration-gate, and automating the decision would contradict the PRD.
